title: United Airlines 2885
summary: A DC-8 cargo flight crashed during takeoff from Detroit after an unauthorized seat swap placed an insufficiently trained flight engineer at the controls. The aircraft pitched nose-up to an excessive attitude, causing engine surges, wing bank, and a stall at approximately 1000 feet altitude. Investigation revealed the horizontal stabilizer was set to 7.5 units nose-up trim, likely due to inadequate pre-takeoff checklist procedures during the confusion of the crew change.
probable_cause: An excessively high stabilizer trim setting of 7.5 units nose-up during takeoff. Contributing factors included an unauthorized flight engineer performing the takeoff, the flight engineer's inadequate training and previous failed proficiency checks, and the captain's failure to correct the situation or prevent the unauthorized seat swap.

events.text: Flight engineer performed takeoff from Detroit contrary to FAA and company rules after unauthorized seat swap
Aircraft nose pitched up to unusually high position with stabilizer trim at 7.5 units nose-up
Temporary engine surges occurred; witnesses on ground reported occasional fire eruptions from engines
Aircraft began gradual right roll as wings reached almost 90-degree bank angle
Aircraft at 1000 ft altitude stalled and fell to the ground, exploding on impact

notes: Sections read: SYNOPSIS, History of the Flight, Personnel Information, Human Performance analysis, and Conclusions from NTSB AAR-83-07. Primary cause: flightcrew's failure to follow checklist procedures and detect/correct a mistrimmed stabilizer (7.5 units nose-up) before aircraft became uncontrollable. Contributing factors included unauthorized crew seat swap, inadequate flight engineer training, and crew fatigue. FDR non-functional. Reaffirmed four prior safety recommendations (A-82-64 through A-82-67) regarding digital flight recorder installation.

recommendations.text: Installation of suitable digital flight recorder systems on air carrier aircraft
